title: Called effect
sub: “Damage” as a separate effect: “Strike” passes it the target and a number.
start: you already have “Strike”: it takes 5 hit points off the target by itself and does not call “Damage”. You will create “Damage” separately and connect it to “Strike”.

called.title: Called effect
called.sum: “Damage” receives a target and a number, takes off hit points and reports how many are left.

call.title: Call
call.sum: On a success “Strike” calls “Damage”. The trial and “Problems” confirmed it.

alone.title: On your own
alone.sum: You built a second effect that others call, and its call, without hints.

called.lead: Many things deal damage: a strike, a trap, poison. We describe it once as the “Damage” effect, and other effects will call it. What is passed to “Damage” — to whom and how much — is set in its “What comes in”.
called.add: In the “Effect library” press the “+” button with “by button”.
called.type: Type the name “Damage” and press Enter.
called.result: “Damage” is created. For now it has one input — “Who acts”.

amount.say: In “What comes in” add a number “Quantity” and mark it “Amount”: this is what is passed to “Damage” as a number.
amount.name: In “Name” type “Quantity” and press Enter.
amount.hint: Without “Amount” “Damage” will not get a number that can be modified. “Amount” is hidden under “more” on the “Quantity” row.

target.say: Make “Strike” pass its own target to “Damage”: for the input “Who acts” in “Damage”, in “Who is it” choose “target — the one chosen at the table or the current one”.
target.hint: Without this, in the “Damage” call “Who acts” will show a red “not passed”.
target.open: In “What comes in” click “Who acts”: the row expands.
target.pick: In “Who is it” choose “target — the one chosen at the table or the current one”.
target.result: “Who acts” arrives by itself: it is the target that “Strike” is currently hitting.

apply.say: Add a “Change”: subtract “Quantity” from “Who acts”. In “Which field” choose “Hit points”.
apply.hint: “Whose” should say “Who acts” and “How” should say “subtract”: that is how they already are.
apply.group: In the group “in this effect” choose “Quantity”.

returns.lead: “Damage” can tell whoever called it how many hit points the target has left — for example, so that “Strike” can check whether it fell.
returns.say: In “What the caller gets back” add a number “Remaining” — the target’s hit points after the damage.
returns.name: In “Name” type “Remaining” and press Enter.
returns.from: In “Taken from” choose “by formula…” and click the field that appears.
returns.pick: Start typing “hit points” and choose “Hit points” in the group of the “Who acts” sheet.
returns.trap: The result is of the kind “yes or no” — choose “number”: any number of hit points can be left.
returns.result: “Remaining” is the target’s hit points after the damage.

call.say: Make “Strike” call “Damage” for 5 on a success.
call.hint: “Who acts” fills in by itself — it is the target. “how it works →” in the call step opens “Damage” itself.
call.add: Open “Strike”. In the “success” branch choose “Damage” in the “+ step” list.
call.five: In the red “Quantity” click the field and type 5.
call.result: On a success “Strike” calls “Damage”: 5 to the target.

drop.say: Delete the old “Change” from the “success” branch: “Damage” now takes off the hit points.
drop.delete: On the “Change” step in the “success” branch press “Delete”.
drop.result: “Strike” no longer has a “Change” of its own.

callName.say: So that the steps below can read “Remaining”, give the call the name “damage”.
callName.hint: Is the call collapsed? In the “success” branch click the call: it expands.
callName.type: Type the name “damage” and press Enter.
callName.result: The call is named “{{name}}”: the steps below see its “Remaining”.

trial.say: Check “Strike” with a trial: with the die “maximum”, “What came out” will show the line {{line}} — the damage went through “Damage”.
trial.result: The trial showed: the damage went through “Damage”.

problems.say: Press the “No problems” button in the header (if something is found, it says “Problems” and a number). There should be no errors: if “Strike” does not pass “Damage” something it needs, the error will appear here.

heal.say: Make a “Heal” effect that adds hit points, and call it from “Strike” on a failure.
heal.goal: “Heal” adds hit points to the sheet passed to it, “Strike” calls it in the “failure” branch, and “Problems” shows no errors.
heal.hint: the “+” button with “by button”, in “What comes in” add a number “Quantity”, in the “Change” set “How” to “add”. In “Strike” under the fork press the button with “failure” and put a call of “Heal” there.
